description: Fixed retrieval-query manifest for E10. Compares two TextExtractor arms (raw / markdownV1) against ONE identical corpus snapshot, embedder, chunk geometry and concurrency. Labels (relevant files + passage criteria) were assigned by reading each document BEFORE any ranking was observed, and are frozen once committed. This file is the single source of truth for the queries; the harness reads it, never the prose.

corpus.scope: Markdown-only (*.md). Includes the large NPR asset assets/riot-data.md (~2.5 MB). Excludes every non-Markdown asset: transcript.json, content.json, info.json, activities.json, properties.json, *.webloc, *.vtt, *.strings, and all images/OCR. No JSON and no OCR assets are indexed.
corpus.notes: Each of the 8 saved items exposes one content.md. riot-data.md is a 9th Markdown file (an asset of the NPR Jan-6 item). Nine files total: top10 recall is uninformative at this size, so scoring uses rank1 / top3 / top5 / MRR only.

fixed_settings.note: Both arms share this exact profile, snapshot, concurrency, batch/bucket, and compute policy. Only the TextExtractor text-extraction mode differs. No format-specific database behavior is introduced. The arm text_extraction values are the exact TextExtractionMode raw values (raw, markdown-v1); the harness preflights every arm mode before any indexing.

metrics.no_answer_handling: For a no-answer probe the harness records the top file groups and their scores (score = 1 - cosine distance) for manual inspection. It does NOT apply a cosine cutoff and makes no automatic pass/fail claim about absence.

labeling.method: relevant_files and passage_criteria were assigned from document content BEFORE any ranking output was seen. File rank is the automatic, authoritative signal. Passage criteria are advisory, human-checkable strings the best-matching passage should contain. The harness runs a best-effort, case-insensitive check of each criterion against the retrieved passage (reconstructed from its source line range) and the stored content preview, and records that result SEPARATELY from file rank.

search.note: Mirrors the real CLI search semantics exactly: fetch limit*3 raw chunk hits (30) then coalesce to limit (10) file groups via SearchResultCoalescer.coalesce. The overfetch pool records overfetch diversity and source ranges WITHOUT changing the coalesced ranking. The harness archives ALL coalesced groups (each with every match and its source range) so file rank can be recomputed independently.

queries.text: How many people were federally charged in the January 6 Capitol riot?

passage_criteria.note: aggregate federal-charge count lives only in the summary

queries.rationale: The aggregate counts (1,575 charged, 1,030 pleaded guilty, median 240 days) appear in the NPR item summary content.md, NOT in the per-defendant riot-data.md. Tests summary-vs-raw-data separation.

queries.text: January 6 defendants affiliated with the American Patriot 3% anti-government militia

passage_criteria.note: group name appears only in the per-defendant records

queries.rationale: The specific militia affiliation is a per-defendant detail found only in the 2.5 MB riot-data.md, not the summary. Probes whether a small relevant passage in a very large file can be retrieved, and whether it coalesces to the right file despite many chunks.
